brief: A landing page for Kettle — fifteen seconds to change a lone developer's mind
vision: In the first screen, the objection is answered: moving off the current tool will not eat a weekend. Not the product category, not the feature list — that objection.
There is one thing to do next and it is obvious. A second call to action, if present, is visibly secondary.
The reader can stop after fifteen seconds and still have the point. Nothing load-bearing sits below where a skimmer stops.
Type has a real hierarchy: one thing is clearly the headline, and body text is set at a size a person reads rather than scans past.
The page is restrained. It is not padded to look substantial with testimonials, logos or sections the brief gave no material for.
code: Self-contained: no external stylesheet, script, font or image, and nothing that would 404 offline.
It does not throw. Nothing in the console at load.
At 375px nothing reaches off the page horizontally, and the layout is genuinely adapted rather than a desktop layout scaled down.
The markup says what things are — a heading is a heading, the primary action is a link or a button — rather than divs carrying meaning through class names.
Whatever interactivity exists is worth its weight. No script that only animates something on scroll.
